sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positive multinomial cells, randomized-instrument support, and target-mass positivity remain distinct conditions. Causal tangent legality additionally requires \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\); both are certified from rational response-type face data.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter then contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; the score mean, covariance, active-face remainder, rational offset, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. The diagonal radius records exactly where all such compact moduli have passed, and no premise constrains a label boundary inserted beyond that radius.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: The Carter comparison spine proves fixed-compact and compatible moving-offset multinomial transfer with separate score, covariance, boundary, and semantic-geometry charges. An escaping-boundary array rules out the global upper minimax implication under compact-uniform assumptions; the valid replacement is a global lower limit plus two-sided convergence on a diagonal expanding lawful window. Effective compatible density remains open. Common-ray averaging proves path-independent incidence operators and translation boundary ratios, but the shared-trace collar attempt does not yet prove safety of every positive-weight candidate, actual face--cone discrepancy decay, translated-uniform tails, or a computable refinement schedule. CertGluePFL and replayable global Gaussian certification therefore remain conditional on ECD.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio theorem compares a fixed positive-cell multinomial experiment with its matched Gaussian experiment, but it neither compares moving causal truth regions nor controls parameters escaping every compact. At recession, common-ray commutativity does not imply that incident face and cone rules are close in Gaussian-weighted loss. The outstanding mathematical gap is an input-computable shared-trace construction that preserves every active semantic label and the separated-risk domain for every positive-weight candidate while controlling translated tails and total refinement complexity.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Exact equality on a geometric face is insufficient when several collar candidates have positive weight nearby, and forward distance monotonicity from one mean is insufficient for canonical normal sections across a branching recession incidence diagram. Compact local asymptotics and effective global recession certification are consequently distinct problems.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer contains Carter's positive-cell specialization, bounded-loss total-variation propagation, finite completed-arrangement stability, fixed-compact and moving-offset transfer, a global certificate-first lower limit, and two-sided expanding-window convergence. The common-ray construction additionally supplies coherent path-independent incidence operators and explicit translation boundary ratios. The unresolved contribution is ECD itself: canonical-section semantic and \(H_r\) preservation, safety of every positive-weight collar candidate, noncircular face--cone discrepancy control, translated-uniform guard and normal-base tails, and refinement counts \(N_j\) with computable schedules satisfying \(N_j/L_j\to0\).

body.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) is used only for bounded-ratio multinomial laws and their matched multivariate normal laws through parameter-independent kernels. The present compact transfer separately handles the fixed score map, covariance replacement, completed-affine-arrangement stability, and moving offsets. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka's 1964 Foelner conditions address a single amenable commuting action; they do not provide a finite input-computable modulus, semantic coverage, separated-risk preservation, or complexity control on a branching recession poset. They therefore do not close ECD.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density remains to be proved or refuted by an encoded counterexample. The shared-trace attempt stops at five precise gaps: canonical normal sections are not known to preserve every active label and \(H_r\); every candidate with positive collar weight is not known to be safe; shared face vertices do not give an overlap identity or a vanishing bound for actual face--cone discrepancies; guard and normal-base tails are not controlled uniformly over translated means; and the refinement complexity \(N_j\) has no explicit bound supporting computable \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) with \(N_j/L_j\to0\). Restricting an already-glued rule to manufacture matching traces would be circular, and constant lower-skeleton extension can activate unsafe candidates. The milliscale four-label certificate therefore also remains open.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand remains the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals. Carter-backed sampled-data claims are compact or expanding-window claims; the original global multinomial value has a proved lower limit but no proved upper limit under the current hypotheses. Common-ray coherence, smoothing, single-chart averaging, and the fixed-library weighted ledger are proved, but no simultaneous recession compatibility modulus is claimed. CertGluePFL termination, its global Gaussian primal--dual certificate, and replayability of certificate-derived windowed rules remain explicitly conditional on ECD.
body.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the correct local decision target on every fixed lawful direction window. Its minimax value is the limit of the explicitly defined expanding-window multinomial values and a lower limit for the original global values. The global unbounded upper limit is not implied by compact-uniform comparison. Likewise, the existing common-ray library is a coherent algebraic recession representation, not yet a compatibility-density theorem: exact mesh traces on faces do not by themselves control all rules mixed in neighboring collars.
